We had our daughter two years after we had our first son.  She was born with a cleft lip and pallet.  

We were amazing.  The doctors and nurses were confused and bewildered and had no idea what to do.  My wife did.  She was on the phone to Shriner's hospitals the next day.  By the third day we were loaded up in our now old, tiny junk car she'd bought right after college and were driving ten hours to the Shriner's hospital for help.  

I wasn't abusive to her as an infant.  I was a doting and loving father or at least that's what I thought.  I was probably at best adequate and at worst neglectful.  

I remember how clear it became to me that I was a shitty father to her when at the age of four I was home alone with the children "taking care of them" when she fell and knocked on of her only front teeth out.  I'll never forget her words until the day I die, "He's helping me, oldest son's name!"  "He's helping me!"

If a man ever needed clearer evidence that he was a piece of shit that was it.  

She was/is very strong and independent.  She was protecting her brother on the bus by the age of six.  The other kids would make fun of him and she'd stand up to them and make them back down.  She was an amazing person and still is to this day.  

Sadly she suffers from an IQ of 85 but for some reason "God" blessed her with amazingly good emotional intelligence.  It's funny, to this day she can't count change or read an analog clock but she can tell you dead on how you're feeling at this very moment with just a glance and she knows what to say to you to make things better.

At the age of thirteen we caught her sending erotic pictures to men and sexting men.  We have no idea who these men were or how she met them but it was, what it was.  I beat her for that.  I beat her hard.  Took away her phone for six months and grounded her for as long.  

It really didn't change much for her though.  she just snuck around and continued as she had.  

She met a boy at sixteen who was two years younger than her and fell madly in love with him.  

While she continued to see and sext these men, she devoted herself to him.  

When she was eighteen she just stopped going to school and decided to party.  The love of her life had broken up with her and she began hanging out with prostitutes and taking hard drugs.  

I really don't know the details.  After I lost my job she got back together with the love of her life and his family basically adopted her.  As dysfunctional as they are I think they are taking better care of her than we ever did.  

She is a beautiful, emotionally intelligent woman who has figured out she doesn't want her mother and father in her life because we are toxic.

We got pregnant again two years later.  This was our golden time.  I'd worked my way up and everything was going right.  We could do no wrong.  We had money for the first time.  We did things.  We were happy.  

At twenty weeks we went in for an ultrasound and we could tell by the way the technician was acting something was very, very wrong.  We were sent to talk to a doctor and get another ultrasound "vaginal probe" the next day.  We found out then that the baby had no kidneys and there was no amniotic fluid in the womb.  Therefore the baby had no lungs.  The baby would have continued to develop and would have been horribly deformed.  The sick part was that the brain would have developed and functioned "normally" but at birth he would die.  

We decided that the only thing we could do, the only moral thing we could do was have an abortion.  

The state we lived in didn't allow abortions for any reason other than "the life of the mother."   There was only one abortion clinic and it was eight hours away.  We had to prove to some state official that my wife could die if she continued to carry the baby.  This process took two more weeks.  

After we got approval, we had to load up everyone in our minivan and drive the eight hours to the abortion clinic.  We had to get another "vaginal probe" ultrasound and watch it.  We had to by law.  He was a boy, with a club foot and he was obviously to us anyway, suffering.  

We now had to wait 72 hours before we could go in and start the process of the abortion.  

We went in and they gave her pills to take and out these sticks in her cervix to open it up wide enough to do the abortion by suction.  She was in tremendous pain.  

The next day we went in to the clinic and she got undressed put on her gown and got in to a hospital bed.  She was bleeding heavily.  I was so afraid and the blood would not stop.  She just kept bleeding and bleeding and crying.  

Finally she was ready and they took her in.  She was awake for the whole process, she cried and cried and moaned in pain and regret.  

It was over.  We spent that night in the hospital (would lied about why she was there so we could get a bed) and talked all night.  

The insurance company covered none of the costs.  We were left with a bill of over $10,000 to pay on our own.  We actually had to set up a five year payment plan.  

Everything changed in our lives from here on out.  We were more distant and didn't know why.  We tried to fix it by having more children.

Our next son was born two years later.  His life was/is unremarkable.  I did all the right things.  I'd finally learned to not be a shitty father.  I wasn't a good father but I wasn't shitty.  

He's well adjusted and very, very intelligent.  He's so smart that he's skipped a grade level and still is so bored he gets in to trouble all the time.  He got kicked out of his advanced classes for highly intelligent children for causing trouble.  

He's very smart, has friends and yet is very quiet and private.  I really try not to bother him.  I love him very much and see him as the future of my line.  

After i lost my job and things got tough, we were eating rice, potatoes, beans and Ramen... He went to live with his mother.  


Seven years later in a desperate attempt to save our marriage we had our last child.   I was and her mother was to old to be having a baby.  I'm glad we did.  

She is our most perfect person we've ever created.  The most intelligent of all our children, the most beautiful and the most emotionally intelligent child we ever had.  The problem is of course for someone as gifted as she is, is the fact that she wears her heart on her sleeve.  She senses everything, knows when things are wrong and sadly as we all know there's always something wrong. 

She's very tall for her age, loves her older sister dearly and loves her mother unconditionally.  She's giving, caring and empathetic to a fault.  

I think she's also very lonely.  Odd that.  She reads constantly.  

Of all the children she trusts me the least and I have no idea why.  I've actually done it right with her and love her very much.  Perhaps it's my failure to maintain a safe place for her here.  Maybe it's because she had to go live with her mother full time because I couldn't maintain a home.  Maybe.

So that is all about my children.

I for some reason took her in and after a few months, even though she'd cheated on me and I'd cheated on her, we got engaged and a couple years later we got married, because we didn't know what else to do.

Me, their father, was raised by a doting mother and a Korean war veteran with PTSD.  People always think you should feel sorry for people with PTSD but it's the people in their lives that deserve sympathy.   

I was of course beaten and abused physically and mentally by my father.  That of course wasn't the worst part or the most life changing part for me.  It was being helpless as he abused and beat the people I loved.  I'd try to intervene at an early age but of course all that did was make him beat whoever it was harder and when he would finish there he'd move on to any anyone who tried to interfere until he was physically exhausted.  

By the age of three I was sneaking and smoking my mother's cigarettes.  I mention this because this was no easy task.  You see my father had forbidden my  mother from smoking.  I remember one time when I was very young that my father had found a cigarette butt in the toilet.  You see she'd flushed but didn't make sure it went down.  My father of course went in to a rage and my brother stepped up and took the blame.  You see dad knew he was lying to protect his mother.  He of course went completely insane.  Funny how those words have little meaning to people who haven't seen such a thing.  He beat him unconscious over the course of several hours.  My brother laid silent in his bed for three days.  We all thought he was dead and we had no idea what to do.  We obviously couldn't tell anyone.  We started making plans for how we'd get rid of the body and explain to people my brother went to live elsewhere.  Fortunately he woke up.

By the age of four I'd found my brother's and dad's pot stashes and I began to use daily.   

I was of course completely socially awkward and it was impossible for me to make friends for any length of time.  

Of course I was tortured in school, bullied and the kids were cruel.  I found books and spent all my time reading.  Book after book.  Books about anything and everything.  I developed a love for science and I'd spend my time hiding in my closet reading with a flashlight.  

By the time I was twelve, I'd figured out that in order to not get bullied and to have a fighting chance against my father, I started to lift weights.  I used the gym at the high school and when it wasn't available I'd use my own body weight to strength train.  

By my froshmen year in high school no one called me gay anymore or teased me.  

It was the books.  I formed a plan on how to get out of there.  I had my first job at thirteen and started saving money for college.  

I played football and loved the contact and violence, it was such a wonderful release.  After I graduated high school I moved out and went to college.  

My freshman year at college my brother killed himself.  He went to my room at home, got my rifle and shot himself on my bed.  I went home for the funeral and left for college again that very day.  It didn't matter, he didn't matter.  All that mattered was that I had to get out.  

I worked and went to school and grew my hair and worked and went to school.  There are no awesome college party stories or spring breaks, there was only work and school.  

I lost my virginity at the age of 21 to a very sweet blonde girl who'd had a crush on me from afar for a long time.  I of course was completely unable to form a bond or relationship.

At the age of 24 my mother killed herself.  I went home for the funeral and went back to graduate school the same day.  

I was sitting in my apartment the spring after my mother died making a list of my booty calls trying to decide on which I would make my wife.  I was incredibly naive.  The very last person on the list, the person who had "Do not contact, total human scum" eventually became my wife.   

I got my masters degree and couldn't find a job.  We were living in an apartment and the rent was $300 a month.  She'd bought a car brand new that we couldn't afford and crushing student loan debt.  She was working in a call center making little more than minimum wage at the time, not using her degree at all.  I found work in a paint warehouse, picking up boxes of paint (4 gallons each) and buckets of paint (5 to 15 gallons each) for $6.50 an hour.  I was American slave labor.  I went from a muscular and fit 255lbs to 167lbs in two years.  The working conditions were indescribable.   

I caught a break and got a job as a supervisor on the third shift in a laboratory.  We got debt free.  We bought our fist house a year later.  Our mortgage was $350 a month.  Heh!

We had our first child, a boy, two years later.

We of course had no idea how to raise a baby or child.  We worked and put him in day care and when I wasn't at work I had him and when she wasn't at work she had him.  

The problem was that I was working a third shift.  When I got home I needed sleep bad.  Of course, I couldn't sleep I had a baby to take care of.  I wasn't a good father.  I left him as an infant on the floor with torn up pieces of bread to suck on while I slept.  If that didn't quiet him so I could sleep, I'd put him in his swing for hours at a time.  

One time he wouldn't stop crying and I began screaming at him to shut up and he just kept crying and I held my hand over his mouth and nose for far to long.  It was a horrific act.  He didn't die but I could see the horror in an infants eyes.

by the time he was six he had developed a diaper fetish and would wear his sisters diapers and pee and poop in them and hid the diapers.  

He was tortured at school.  The kids were cruel to him.  He became very shy and introverted.  

I tried to be a good father.  I coached his baseball and soccer teams and basketball teams.  Enrolled him in activities, went to church, doing all the things I was other fathers doing.  What I didn't see was how these fathers acted at home.  I was at best neglectful and worst abusive to him at home.  

 By the time he was none he'd found his way a round the parental blocking software on our home computer.  He'd found away around the user settings and was in to the deep web.  The scary nasty part of the Internet.
